items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The lowest of men are the context of concealment
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and under what condition may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person who has been tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
The chapter is the fifth
items.inference: The fifth chapter of the work that emerged from Candradvīpa concludes here.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the work that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has the speaker gained through the grace of the lord of Kaulas?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Grace is the means of understanding
The determination of Kaula has become known
items.inference: By the lord of Kaulas' grace, the speaker has come to know the determination of Kaula.
items.plain_english: O lord of Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What identity and essential nature are being asked about regarding the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks to know who the declared soul is and what its essential nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker asks into what the soul dissolves and requests a full explanation of all this.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality identified as that soul?
premises: That reality is supreme
That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The ultimate reality is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and the individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That soul is identified as haṃsa
That soul is identified as the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, the individual constituted by power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated within living beings?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
Living beings are the locus
The air is situated in all beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement of saṃsthitam with vāyuḥ is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What status is attributed to the soul immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
The moment of leaving is decisive
It is then called supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is declared to be the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and perceived according to traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
The goddess is addressed
It has come down through traditional succession
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as something received through traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What minimal reception of this teaching is said to be effective for the practitioner?
premises: The teaching can be merely known
The teaching can be merely heard
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even mere knowledge or mere hearing of this teaching is presented as effective.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, and by merely hearing it...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is undertaken for six months
The practitioner engages in the ochre discipline
The result is freedom from bondage
items.inference: One who practices this discipline for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to renunciant discipline rather than a literal robe.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state free from bondage.

items.question: What two benefits result from the prescribed practice for the accomplished practitioner?
premises: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with yogis is achieved
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: Bhairavī is addressed
The practice of the soul is the topic
This teaching has been told to her
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching properly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a resolved mind.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one endowed with all states and of resolved mind.

items.question: What essential Kaula teaching must not be given indiscriminately?
premises: There is a Kaula essence
It is the origin associated with the yoginīs
This essence must not be given
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, the origin associated with the yoginīs, must not be given.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, the origin of the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the speaker's body is claimed after receiving knowledge?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now pure
items.inference: The speaker claims that her body, once struck by ignorance, is now pure.
uncertainties: deham appears in accusative form but functions as subject in this context.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker now wishes to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired teaching is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker wishes to hear the auspicious teaching on overcoming or deceiving time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the possibility of destroying death?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
There is no doubt
Death can be destroyed
items.inference: The teacher assures without doubt that the means by which death is destroyed will be explained.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: What intense experience at the source of nectar affects even the wise practitioner?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
The essence of juice is involved
Even the wise one experiences burning
items.inference: Even a wise practitioner experiences a burning sensation at the tip of nectar through its essence.
uncertainties: The physiological referent of amṛta+agraṃ is technical and context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Even the wise one burns at the tip of nectar with the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic action with the breath at the palate-root is prescribed for practice?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate
The breath is directed there
The breath should be drawn in slowly
items.inference: The practitioner should place the breath at the root of the tongue and palate and slowly drink it in.
items.plain_english: Placing the breath at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink it in.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When this practice is maintained for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for one established in this practice?
premises: The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents
Poison would normally enter the body
In this case poison does not enter
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body of such a practitioner.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
